title: Runner 10's handoff says to set a one-time check-in at each ready mark; no new tool
why: Debt named by runner 10 (09:07 CST Nov 14, relayed): after a gap with no event, a green ready run waited unmerged. Case: #3238, ready run 43604213305 green since 08:48:39 CST, merged 09:06:14: 17 min, because runner 10 had no wake after 08:30 (its own account, logged in its handoff; n=1). Rescoped 09:17 CST Nov 14 from the coordinator (09:08, relayed): root rule git-ci-wait-checks-in already says a session that waits on CI sets a one-time check-in when it starts to wait, so this is runner 10 not following an existing rule, not a missing rule. A handoff line is the right size unless the same miss recurs. The coordinator does not know whether runner 10 sets a check-in per ready mark and is asking it. Earlier samples on the record that are not this miss: #3377 (green 06:15 to merge call 06:44 was inside the merge tool) and runner 10's session idle 05:41 to 06:03. If it recurs: a guard needs an incident (the miss recurred) and its cost; a candidate is the merge tool printing "ready run green N min, not merged" at the next call; not built, unmeasured. Done when: runner 10's handoff carries the line and no green ready run waits over 10 min across the next 5 merges (a count to take from the merge log; unmeasured now).
